tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

3	*Last updated: 2026-06-25*

7	Scope: price feeds & pricebooks, price display & tax, sale & markdown pricing, multi-currency & FX, VIC/customer-group pricing, and Global-e pricing & cart handoff. The promotions engine (coupons, stacking) lives in [promotions.md](promotions.md).

PRC-03 and PRC-07 confirmed Emma/Rebecca 2026-06-24. Open/challenged items are listed in section 7: PRC-13, PRC-45, PRC-46 (open); Platinum rate (PRC-17), final-sale attribute (PRC-12), Global-e VIC catalogue pricing (PRC-43), GiveX currency coverage (PRC-53).*
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. Price Feeds & Pricebooks (PRC-01 – PRC-04, PRC-34 – PRC-35)
14	
15	- Product pricing consumed from AP21 via MuleSoft, including current selling price, original/RRP price, and markdown status. Mapped to SFCC pricebook fields (PRC-01, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma; assumption is RetailPrice stored as an additional price field; EK query outstanding on who owns final RetailPrice functional confirmation)
16	- Both full and delta price feeds supported from AP21 via MuleSoft. Price changes in the delta are expected to be minimal; pricing and product ingestion are treated as distinct processes (PRC-02, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
17	- **Base RRP pricebooks per currency** (minimum: AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) consumed from AP21 via MuleSoft into SFCC — source of truth for domestic prices and calculation base for FX-derived international markets (PRC-34, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
18	- **Fixed pricelists per Global-e market** consumed from AP21 via MuleSoft into SFCC. CS query: confirm fixed pricelists are accessible once imported (today appended from SFTP marketing feeds) (PRC-35, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
19	- Future-dated markdown pricing activation via MuleSoft — date and time supported (not date only), so sale pricing can go live at a precise datetime. Confirmed 2026-06-24 (RJ/Mani, based on Billy's AP21 feedback). Timezone mapping: one default timezone per storefront; times in local pricebooks are expressed in the storefront's timezone; MuleSoft is responsible for converting and setting the appropriate time in SFCC (PRC-03, confirmed — signed off by Emma/Rebecca 2026-06-24)
20	- Pricebooks for multiple currencies per regional site (PRC-04, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 2. Price Display & Tax (PRC-05 – PRC-08)
25	
26	- AU and EU sites display prices **inclusive of tax** (GST/VAT included). Same base price across all EU countries — differing VAT rates handled in the background (PRC-05, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
27	- US site displays prices **exclusive of tax**; Avalara calculates per-state tax added at checkout (PRC-06, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
28	- Bulk assignment of tax class to products supported — tax class driven by AP21 taxonomy ID (derived from product category, configured by finance) fed into SFCC via MuleSoft; no manual bulk updates required. Avalara covers AU, EU, US, and UK domestic storefronts for go-live. International storefronts (HK, ME, US Int'l, EU Int'l) handled through Global-e. HS code handling may still need further exploration but is not a go-live blocker (PRC-07, confirmed — signed off by Emma/Rebecca 2026-06-24)
29	- Product prices displayed consistently in storefront currency across PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, wishlist, recommended tiles, and checkout (PRC-08, PRC-33)
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 3. Sale & Markdown Pricing (PRC-09 – PRC-13)
34	
35	- Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, and order history. Note (DR): sale items are usually excluded from recommendations via a manual rule (PRC-09)
36	- Business users can schedule sale pricing to go live at a specified future date and time. Category pre-merchandised; team QCs via live-preview before go-live (PRC-10, confirmed)
37	- **SFCC native storefront preview** supports QC of scheduled pricing and category changes before go-live, including preview for specific customer groups — scoped to SFCC OOTB preview, no custom build (PRC-11, confirmed)
38	- Final sale flag supported on products (PRC-12, confirmed). Assumption: `is_returnable` drives returnable status, `final_sale` drives front-end final-sale messaging. Attribute distinction and AP21 derivation still to be confirmed — see Open Items. No final-sale icon in design yet
39	- Price display behaviour based on AP21 `MarkdownStatus` values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) — open: Zimmermann to confirm what each value means and what storefront behaviour it should drive (PRC-13, open)

41	---
42	
43	## 4. Multi-Currency & Regional Pricebooks (PRC-14, PRC-36 – PRC-43, PRC-47 – PRC-52)
44	
45	- Country/currency selector shows prices in the currency configured for the customer's selected shipping country (PRC-14, confirmed). Note (RJ): the country selector is not present on the AU site
46	- **Country-to-currency mapping** configurable in SFCC Business Manager without code deployment (PRC-36, PRC-52)
47	- Per currency, the system stores the **conversion approach**: (a) Base RRP, (b) Fixed Pricelist from AP21, (c) Fixed FX rate from base, or (d) Dynamic FX rate from base (PRC-37)
48	- **Nightly job** loads Global-e pricing into SFCC: FX rates, price coefficients, and rounding rules (PRC-38)
49	- Pricebooks generated from Global-e pricing data and imported into SFCC (PRC-39)
50	- Target-currency price calculation: `base pricebook price × FX rate × country coefficient × product-class coefficient` (PRC-40)
51	- Calculated prices included in the SFCC search index for price-based filters and sort on PLP/search (PRC-41)
52	- All promotion calculations executed in the customer's selected ship-to currency (PRC-42)
53	- **Currency display formatting** per locale: symbol position, decimal places (including zero-decimal currencies), thousand separator, minus-sign for refunds (PRC-47)
54	- **FX rate locked at order placement** and applied to any refund at the same locked rate — refund in target currency equals original charged amount (PRC-48)
55	- **Currency rounding strategy** per currency (e.g. nearest whole AED, 2 decimal EUR, 0 decimal JPY); applied at line-item level before tax/promotion stacking (PRC-49)
56	- Business Manager interface for authorised users: view conversion approach per currency, set/change conversion approach, view current FX rate with last-updated timestamp and feed status; read-only access for merchandising team (PRC-50)
57	- Bulk import/export of currency config via SFCC Site Import/Export, OCAPI, or deployment scripts — technical users only (PRC-51)
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)
62	
63	Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (not cart-only discounts). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards.
64	
65	| Customer group | Discount |
66	|---|---|
67	| Gold VIC | Permanent 10% off all non-sale products |
68	| Platinum VIC | Permanent discount — rate TBC (Zimmermann to confirm) |
69	| VIC early access | Flat 30% off before public sale goes live; removed before public sale |
70	| Advent customers | e.g. 50% off during Advent events |
71	| PR companies and investors | Configured discount |
72	
73	- **Customer group discounts do NOT stack on sale items** (PRC-18, revised per DR): sale items are excluded from promotion set-ups. Example: a Gold VIC customer receives 10% off full-price items, but if they add a sale product to cart they get the sale price only — no extra 10% on top. The system must continue to support this exclusion.
74	- Configurable priority rules in SFCC Business Manager (e.g. Gold VIC 10% excludes gift cards and items already on sale) (PRC-19)
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 6. Global-e Pricing & Cart Handoff (PRC-15 – PRC-16, PRC-43 – PRC-46, PRC-53 – PRC-55)
79	
80	- DDP/DDU duties messaging on PDP per country — configurable per country (PRC-15)
81	- SFCC passes a **complete cart to Global-e** in the customer's target currency at international checkout, including: all line items with quantities, prices in target currency, all applied promotions and coupon codes, Retail Rewards, gift cards, and a placeholder/dummy shipping method. Global-e adds actual shipping charges and processes payment (PRC-16, PRC-43). Note (DR): current M2 implementation has limitations — Global-e does not accept M2 catalogue promotions where the discount price appears on PLP/PDP for logged-in customer groups. 82	- **Coupon codes**: validation occurs in SFCC; discount values passed to Global-e in cart payload — Global-e does not call back to SFCC to re-validate (PRC-46, open — workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off comment conditions delivery on Global-e being able to apply and validate coupons: "This will be delivered only if Global-e can support." Treated as open until Global-e confirms capability; see Open Items)
83	- **Gift card webhooks**: GiveX gift card validate/redeem/refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44)
84	- **Retail Rewards at Global-e checkout**: applied after promotions (PRC-45, open — RJ challenges the "max 1 reward per order" limit: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order". Max-rewards-per-order count to be confirmed; see Open Items)
85	- Customers can purchase GiveX gift cards as products at Global-e checkout; provisioned in GiveX via existing middleware after payment (PRC-53, confirmed). Note (RJ): for Global-e regions gift cards are digital-only; currency coverage to be confirmed — see Open Items
86	- **Daily Global-e catalogue export job**: generates and uploads a product catalogue CSV to Global-e via SFTP for product-level restrictions, VAT rates, and HS code assignments (PRC-54)
87	- Authentication configured between SFCC and Global-e for all API calls (PRC-55)
88	
89	---

94	- Final sale vs. is_returnable attribute distinction and AP21 derivation — Zimmermann to confirm; no final-sale icon in design yet (PRC-12, otherwise confirmed)
95	- AP21 MarkdownStatus values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) and storefront behaviour — Zimmermann to confirm (PRC-13)

97	- Fixed pricelists once imported via MuleSoft — CS query: confirm in-system accessibility vs. today's SFTP append (PRC-35, otherwise confirmed)
98	- **Coupon codes at Global-e checkout** — workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off comment is conditional: "RJ / Mani need to confirm that the coupon can be applied and is validated through Global-e. This will be delivered only if Global-e can support." Confirm with Global-e that the SFCC cartridge can apply and validate coupon codes before this requirement is treated as confirmed (PRC-46)
99	- Global-e SFCC cartridge support for customer-group catalogue prices at international checkout (PRC-43) — confirm with Global-e; Zimmermann to confirm current M2 workaround for VIC pricing at Global-e checkout
100	- Retail Rewards count at Global-e checkout — requirement states max 1 reward per order; RJ challenges: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order". Confirm max-per-order before implementing (PRC-45)

## 1. Price Feeds & Pricebooks (PRC-01 – PRC-04, PRC-34 – PRC-35)

Mapped to SFCC pricebook fields (PRC-01, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma; assumption is RetailPrice stored as an additional price field; EK query outstanding on who owns final RetailPrice functional confirmation)

- **Base RRP pricebooks per currency** (minimum: AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) consumed from AP21 via MuleSoft into SFCC — source of truth for domestic prices and calculation base for FX-derived international markets (PRC-34, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)

## 2. Price Display & Tax (PRC-05 – PRC-08)

## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)

Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (not cart-only discounts). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards.

| Customer group | Discount |
|---|---|
| Gold VIC | Permanent 10% off all non-sale products |

- **Customer group discounts do NOT stack on sale items** (PRC-18, revised per DR): sale items are excluded from promotion set-ups. Example: a Gold VIC customer receives 10% off full-price items, but if they add a sale product to cart they get the sale price only — no extra 10% on top. The system must continue to support this exclusion.
- Configurable priority rules in SFCC Business Manager (e.g. Gold VIC 10% excludes gift cards and items already on sale) (PRC-19)

---

## 6. Global-e Pricing & Cart Handoff (PRC-15 – PRC-16, PRC-43 – PRC-46, PRC-53 – PRC-55)

- DDP/DDU duties messaging on PDP per country — configurable per country (PRC-15)
- SFCC passes a **complete cart to Global-e** in the customer's target currency at international checkout, including: all line items with quantities, prices in target currency, all applied promotions and coupon codes, Retail Rewards, gift cards, and a placeholder/dummy shipping method. Global-e adds actual shipping charges and processes payment (PRC-16, PRC-43). Note (DR): current M2 implementation has limitations — Global-e does not accept M2 catalogue promotions where the discount price appears on PLP/PDP for logged-in customer groups. Open (25.05): confirm with Global-e whether the SFCC cartridge supports honouring customer-group catalogue prices at Global-e checkout; if not currently honoured in M2, Zimmermann to confirm how these VIC/customer-group customers are receiving their discounts at international checkout today (e.g. configured directly in Global-e).

1	# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.
6	
7	PWA responsibilities:
8	
9	- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
10	- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
11	- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
12	- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
13	- Handling the order-completion return path
14	
15	Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.
16	
17	## 2. Checkout ownership matrix
18	
19	| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
20	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
21	| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
22	| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
23	| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
24	| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
25	| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
26	| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
27	| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
28	| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |
29	
30	Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.
31	
32	> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.
33	
34	## 3. Browser-side architecture
35	
36	```
37	Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
38	        │
39	        ▼
40	PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived

77	        │
78	        ▼

80	Payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
81	        │

87	continue to show the SFCC order number.

90	- **Pre-checkout currency display.** Target-currency prices are read from the SFCC Global-e-derived price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart.

106	- **Return path.** On order completion Global-e signals the parent frame via `postMessage`.
107	  The `postMessage` triggers an AJAX call from the parent frame to SFCC `orderCreate()` (see the flow diagram above for the full sequence).
108	  The PWA's `window` `"message"` event listener must enforce three conditions before acting on any message:
109	  1. **`event.origin`** matches the confirmed Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1).
110	  2. **`event.source`** equals the checkout `<iframe>` element's `contentWindow` — prevents other windows on the same trusted origin from triggering order completion.
111	  3. **Message schema** matches the expected Global-e payload shape — reject and ignore any message that does not conform.
112	  After all three checks pass:
113	  - Validate `orderRef` from the payload matches the expected Global-e format (`GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) before using it. Reject and ignore the message if it does not match.
114	  - Construct the confirmation URL using `URLSearchParams` (or equivalent URL-safe encoding) rather than direct string interpolation — e.g. `new URLSearchParams({ orderRef }).toString()` — to prevent injection via a malformed payload value.

116	  The international order confirmation email is sent by Global-e; the PWA owns only the on-page confirmation display (CFD-071).

119	
120	| Credential                         | Where used                                                     | Sensitivity                        |
121	| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
122	| Global-e Merchant ID               | Embedded in handoff request                                    | Public                             |
123	| Global-e API key and shared secret | Server-side only (SFCC → Global-e and Global-e webhook → SFCC) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
124	
125	## 5. Data exchanged
126	
127	**Browser / iframe → Global-e (client-side inputs):**
128	
129	- Shopper IP and device user agent (passed by the browser)
130	- Pre-selected destination country (locked once inside the iframe)
131	- Order reference for return-webhook correlation
132	
133	**SFCC → Global-e (SendCart server-side payload):**
134	
135	- Cart line items (SKU, quantity, target-currency price)
136	- Guest email (via `globale.getGuestEmail` hook — pre-populates shopper email in the iframe)
137	- Saved addresses for logged-in shoppers (via `globale.getCustomerAddresses`)
138	- Didomi consent state mapped to Global-e's 0/1/2 scale (via `globale.getCookieConsent`)
139	- Marketing opt-in and direct communication consent flags (via `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` / `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant`)
140	
141	**Global-e → Browser (return):** `postMessage` event to the parent frame triggering `orderCreate()`, after which the parent navigates to the Zimmermann confirmation route.
142	
143	**Runtime session data available to the PWA:**
144	
145	Global-e writes these SFCC session custom attributes on every storefront request after initialisation.
146	The PWA can read these from the SFCC session to determine country/currency context before handoff.
147	
148	| Attribute         | Type    | Description                                  | Example |
149	| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- |
150	| `geCountry`       | String  | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2)   | `GB`    |
151	| `geIsOperated`    | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `true`  |
152	| `geCurrency`      | String  | Currency ISO3 for the selected country       | `GBP`   |
153	| `gePriceStrategy` | String  | Pricing strategy (`DYNAMIC` or `FIXED`)      | `FIXED` |
154	
155	Global-e also sets a `GlobalE_Data` cookie (available client-side) with four fields that map to session attributes:
156	`countryISO` → `geCountry`, `cultureCode` → `geCulture`, `currencyCode` → `geCurrency`, `apiVersion` → `geApiVersion`.
157	Note that `geCulture` and `geApiVersion` are session attributes written by Global-e but are not listed in the table above — they are only surfaced via the cookie.
158	
159	## 6. Performance and loading strategy

161	- Pre-checkout prices come from standard SFCC product/price API responses. No extra Global-e network request sits on the PDP or PLP critical path.
162	- The handoff route embeds the Global-e iframe post-interaction; iframe load latency does not affect parent-page LCP.

# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.

PWA responsibilities:

- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
- Handling the order-completion return path

Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.

## 2. Checkout ownership matrix

| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |

Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.

> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
        │
        ▼
PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived
price books (calculated by the nightly feed) and format it per locale
        │
        ▼
Add to cart — basket persists in SFCC in storefront currency
        │
        ▼
Checkout CTA — PWA calls SFCC to assemble the complete cart payload in the
shopper's target currency (per PRC-34..42)
        │
        ▼
SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side) — "SendCart" — and returns a
`cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side. SFCC also calls
`basket.reserveInventory()` before the SendCart request (default hold: 30 min).
        │
        ▼
PWA renders a Zimmermann checkout route that embeds the Global-e checkout
inside an iframe using the `cartToken`. The shopper remains on www.zimmermann.com
(parent frame); the iframe loads from Global-e's checkout origin.
        │
        ▼
Inside the iframe Global-e collects shipping address, payment, duties, and tax.
When the shopper clicks "Place Order", Global-e calls the SFCC
`Globale-ValidateCart` endpoint to check stock against SFCC inventory.
If stock is insufficient the shopper sees a popup and is redirected to cart —
no order is created on either side.
        │
        ▼
After validation passes, Global-e sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame.
The parent frame makes an AJAX request to SFCC `orderCreate()`, which converts
the basket to an SFCC order with status **Created**. If this call fails (session
expiry, stock change) Global-e's retry mechanism falls back to the
`SendOrderToMerchant` path to recreate and place the order.
        │
        ▼
Global-e calls SFCC's `SendOrderToMerchant` endpoint seconds later to enrich
the order with full international transaction data. Order status → **New**.
        │
        ▼
After fraud screening passes, Global-e calls SFCC's `PerformPayment` endpoint.
Payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
        │
        ▼
Order completion: the PWA navigates the parent frame to the Zimmermann
confirmation route, fetches the order from SFCC, and renders the confirmation.
The order number shown to shoppers is the Global-e order number
(format: `GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`); SFCC domestic orders
continue to show the SFCC order number.
```

- **Pre-checkout currency display.** Target-currency prices are read from the SFCC Global-e-derived price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart.
  SFCC holds these price books, regenerated nightly from Global-e's FX, coefficient, and rounding feed (PRC-34, PRC-38..40).
  Calculated prices are also in the SFCC search index so price filters and sort work on PLP and search results (PRC-41).
  The PWA does not convert prices client-side — it formats the SFCC-supplied target-currency price per locale (symbol position, decimal places including zero-decimal currencies, thousand separator) per PRC-47.
  HK and ME follow the same pattern: prices are read from HKD and AED SFCC price books, not from a Global-e client-side widget.
  No Global-e client-side script is needed to display pricing.

- **DDP/DDU duties messaging.** Shown on PDP per destination country, configurable per country (PRC-15). The data source for this flag (SFCC product attribute vs. Global-e price book field) is not specified in the PRDs — confirm with the integration team before implementing.

- **Handoff payload.** SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency at handoff — line items, quantities, target-currency prices, applied promotions, coupons, Retail Rewards, and gift cards (PRC-16).
  Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from the iframe onwards.

- **Iframe embed.** The Global-e checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route. The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive must list the Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1). Iframe height is managed via Global-e's `postMessage` contract.

- **Shipping country lock.** The shipping country is determined by the country selector pre-checkout and cannot be changed inside the Global-e iframe (REG-028).

- **Return path.** On order completion Global-e signals the parent frame via `postMessage`.
  The `postMessage` triggers an AJAX call from the parent frame to SFCC `orderCreate()` (see the flow diagram above for the full sequence).
  The PWA's `window` `"message"` event listener must enforce three conditions before acting on any message:
  1. **`event.origin`** matches the confirmed Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1).
  2. **`event.source`** equals the checkout `<iframe>` element's `contentWindow` — prevents other windows on the same trusted origin from triggering order completion.
  3. **Message schema** matches the expected Global-e payload shape — reject and ignore any message that does not conform.
  After all three checks pass:
  - Validate `orderRef` from the payload matches the expected Global-e format (`GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) before using it. Reject and ignore the message if it does not match.
  - Construct the confirmation URL using `URLSearchParams` (or equivalent URL-safe encoding) rather than direct string interpolation — e.g. `new URLSearchParams({ orderRef }).toString()` — to prevent injection via a malformed payload value.
  - Navigate the parent frame to `/{prefix}/checkout/confirmation?<encoded-params>` and render the confirmation from the SFCC order record.
  The international order confirmation email is sent by Global-e; the PWA owns only the on-page confirmation display (CFD-071).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential                         | Where used                                                     | Sensitivity                        |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Global-e Merchant ID               | Embedded in handoff request                                    | Public                             |
| Global-e API key and shared secret | Server-side only (SFCC → Global-e and Global-e webhook → SFCC) | Secret — never reaches the browser |

## 5. Data exchanged

**Browser / iframe → Global-e (client-side inputs):**

- Shopper IP and device user agent (passed by the browser)
- Pre-selected destination country (locked once inside the iframe)
- Order reference for return-webhook correlation

**SFCC → Global-e (SendCart server-side payload):**

- Cart line items (SKU, quantity, target-currency price)
- Guest email (via `globale.getGuestEmail` hook — pre-populates shopper email in the iframe)
- Saved addresses for logged-in shoppers (via `globale.getCustomerAddresses`)
- Didomi consent state mapped to Global-e's 0/1/2 scale (via `globale.getCookieConsent`)
- Marketing opt-in and direct communication consent flags (via `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` / `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant`)

**Global-e → Browser (return):** `postMessage` event to the parent frame triggering `orderCreate()`, after which the parent navigates to the Zimmermann confirmation route.

**Runtime session data available to the PWA:**

Global-e writes these SFCC session custom attributes on every storefront request after initialisation.
The PWA can read these from the SFCC session to determine country/currency context before handoff.

| Attribute         | Type    | Description                                  | Example |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `geCountry`       | String  | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2)   | `GB`    |
| `geIsOperated`    | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `true`  |
| `geCurrency`      | String  | Currency ISO3 for the selected country       | `GBP`   |
| `gePriceStrategy` | String  | Pricing strategy (`DYNAMIC` or `FIXED`)      | `FIXED` |

Global-e also sets a `GlobalE_Data` cookie (available client-side) with four fields that map to session attributes:
`countryISO` → `geCountry`, `cultureCode` → `geCulture`, `currencyCode` → `geCurrency`, `apiVersion` → `geApiVersion`.
Note that `geCulture` and `geApiVersion` are session attributes written by Global-e but are not listed in the table above — they are only surfaced via the cookie.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- Pre-checkout prices come from standard SFCC product/price API responses. No extra Global-e network request sits on the PDP or PLP critical path.
- The handoff route embeds the Global-e iframe post-interaction; iframe load latency does not affect parent-page LCP.
- Emit `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Global-e checkout origin from the cart page to warm the TLS handshake before the iframe loads.
- Any retained Global-e client-side script (e.g. duties messaging) must be deferred and load after LCP.
- The Global-e team must configure `frame-ancestors` / `X-Frame-Options` to permit embedding under `www.zimmermann.com`.

## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                                                    | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SFCC Global-e-derived price book is missing or stale for a target currency | Show the storefront-currency price with the message "Final pricing in your currency shown at checkout." Do not silently fall back to an SFCC checkout for an international destination — that would route the order through the wrong checkout flow and carries tax / regulatory risk. |
| Handoff fails (Global-e API outage at cart → handoff)                      | Surface a hard error: "International checkout is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." Do not place the order in SFCC.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Return webhook from Global-e to SFCC is delayed                            | Render the confirmation with the order reference and a "Your order is being processed" state. Full details render once SFCC receives the order.                                                                                                                                        |
| Cart total mismatch between SFCC and Global-e at handoff                   | Reject the order; surface a hard error. Never silently adjust totals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## 8. Security

- The Global-e checkout domain is third-party. Cross-site cookies do not propagate — cart context is passed inside the handoff payload, not via cookies.
- The `postMessage` listener in the parent frame must enforce all three checks documented in §3 — `event.origin`, `event.source`, and message schema — plus `orderRef` format validation and URL-safe query encoding before constructing the confirmation URL. See §3 "Return path" for the full requirements.

## 9. Open items

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply:

   - The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers.
   - The `postMessage` trusted sender origin — the vendor guide confirms that the Global-e iframe sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame to trigger `orderCreate()`, but does not specify the exact origin string or the full message schema. The `event.origin` value and message payload shape must be obtained from Global-e directly before the listener can be safely implemented.
     Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order (from SFCC), to decide between full order detail and a "View on tracking page" fallback.
   Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

On `zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net`, a story's **acceptance criteria are in
`customfield_10231`** ("Acceptance Criteria", project-scoped textarea) — **not** in the
description. Fetching only `description` misses them entirely and makes a card look
underspecified when it isn't.

Some issues return it as plain text with `#` list markers; others return **ADF**
(`{type: "doc", version: 1, content: [...]}`) which needs flattening to read. In one
batch, SFCC-315/270/795 came back as ADF and SFCC-250/271/272/275 as plain text.

`jira_search` with `fields=key,summary,customfield_10231` pulls several cards' ACs in one
call, which is much cheaper than per-issue fetches.

Sprint is `customfield_10020` on this instance (see [[project-real-sprint-cadence]]).
Cards are PO-approved and **not edited** — record deviations as a comment instead
(see [[project-cart-bundle-decisions]]).

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'

- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"

 Shopper, 


I want
 to see a message in the cart telling me whether duties and taxes are included in the displayed price or may be payable on delivery, 
so that 
I understand my total cost before proceeding to checkout.
This story covers the cart (bag) text display only. PDP messaging is covered in 
https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-468
. Checkout-level messaging is handled by Global-e and is out of scope. The cart component itself is 
https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-816
.
The cart reads the active Global-e session country and checks it against a configured DDP and DDU country list to determine which message to show. The list is maintained in a single Contentful entry (UI Copy content model), not toggled per individual locale — one update covers all countries in that Terms of Trade group. Message text is also managed in Contentful. No BM configuration or code deployment required to update either the list or the text.
Three Terms of Trade states apply across Global-e international markets:
Hidden DDP — 50 countries. 
Cart text: "Duties and taxes are included in the price displayed"


Duties and taxes are collected by Global-e and embedded in the displayed price. Shopper pays nothing additional on delivery. Four Hidden DDP variants exist; all show the same cart text:

Hidden DDP + 20% CE (5 countries): C

3	description: SFCC basket merge takes higher-of-two by default, not sum; no Zimmermann code merges at all, and the passwordless sign-in route drops it
4	metadata:
5	  type: project
6	---
7	
8	Verified 2026-09-16 against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types and the base template.
9	
10	**`mergeBasket`'s `productItemMergeMode`** is `higher_quantity` (default) | `sum_quantities` |
11	`saved_quantity` | `separate_item`. Default means **guest 2 + account 2 → 2, not 4** — quantities
12	never sum unless the mode is passed explicitly, and it can only be passed at the call site.
13	
14	**Same-product matching** requires all of: shipment · productId · option values · wishlist
15	reference · inventory list id · gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments. Any mismatch
16	copies the item to a **new line item** instead of merging — so one SKU can exceed a per-order cap
17	across two lines without either line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic differentiators are
18	Collect in Boutique (separate shipment) and boutique vs warehouse inventory lists.
19	
20	**Four base call sites**, all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`: `hooks/use-auth-modal`,
21	`pages/login`, `pages/social-login-redirect`, `pages/checkout/partials/contact-info`. The merge is
22	deliberately **login-only, not register** — a new customer's guest basket simply becomes theirs.
23	
24	**No Zimmermann code calls `mergeBasket`**, and `commerce-sdk-react` does not auto-merge (it only
25	defines the mutation). Of `useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s three routes: social redirects through the base
26	page that merges; create-account correctly skips it; **passwordless OTP merges nothing** — so a
27	recurring shopper signing in that way has their guest basket orphaned and **loses their items**.
28	Code-inferred, not yet observed live — prove it before filing.
29	
30	**Why:** any cart/checkout work touching sign-in inherits this. Assuming the server sums, or
31	assuming a merge happens at all, both produce silently wrong baskets.
32	
33	**How to apply:** check what mode a merge call passes before reasoning about quantities, and treat
34	"a guest signed in" as "the basket may have been orphaned" until the passwordless gap is fixed.
35	Related: [[project-cart-bundle-decisions]], [[project-max-order-quantity]].

---
name: project-cart-merge-mechanics
description: SFCC basket merge takes higher-of-two by default, not sum; no Zimmermann code merges at all, and the passwordless sign-in route drops it
metadata:

---

Verified 2026-09-16 against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types and the base template.

**`mergeBasket`'s `productItemMergeMode`** is `higher_quantity` (default) | `sum_quantities` |
`saved_quantity` | `separate_item`. Default means **guest 2 + account 2 → 2, not 4** — quantities
never sum unless the mode is passed explicitly, and it can only be passed at the call site.

**Same-product matching** requires all of: shipment · productId · option values · wishlist
reference · inventory list id · gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments. Any mismatch
copies the item to a **new line item** instead of merging — so one SKU can exceed a per-order cap
across two lines without either line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic differentiators are
Collect in Boutique (separate shipment) and boutique vs warehouse inventory lists.

**Four base call sites**, all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`: `hooks/use-auth-modal`,
`pages/login`, `pages/social-login-redirect`, `pages/checkout/partials/contact-info`. The merge is
deliberately **login-only, not register** — a new customer's guest basket simply becomes theirs.

**No Zimmermann code calls `mergeBasket`**, and `commerce-sdk-react` does not auto-merge (it only
defines the mutation). Of `useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s three routes: social redirects through the base
page that merges; create-account correctly skips it; **passwordless OTP merges nothing** — so a
recurring shopper signing in that way has their guest basket orphaned and **loses their items**.
