1	/*
2	 * Copyright (c) 2021, salesforce.com, inc.
3	 * All rights reserved.
4	 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
5	 * For full license text, see the LICENSE file in the repo root or https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause
6	 */
7	
8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff beyond the TypeScript annotations below and the temporary
12	 * `[overrides]` console.log marker. The `<Stack textAlign={align} ... {...props}>`
13	 * defaults-then-spread prop order is preserved exactly, unchanged from base.
14	 *
15	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
16	 * `display-price` and the `useCurrency`/`app/hooks` barrel are not overridden anywhere in this
17	 * repo (verified by directory listing at time of writing), so both stay on the base
18	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path.
19	 */
20	import React from 'react'
21	import {FormattedMessage, FormattedNumber} from 'react-intl'
22	import {
23	    Stack,
24	    Text,
25	    useBreakpointValue
26	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
27	import {useItemVariant} from '.'
28	import {getPriceData} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils'
29	import DisplayPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price'
30	
31	// See index.tsx's own note on why this is `any` rather than a structural type.
32	type SfccVariant = any
33	
34	type PricePerItemProps = {
35	    currency: string
36	    // Deviation from the base file (same labelled-comment convention as
37	    // product-view/index.tsx:659-661/1019-1022): base PropTypes declares this as optional
38	    // (`PropTypes.number`, no `.isRequired`), but both real call sites below it — the only two
39	    // in this file — only ever render <PricePerItem> from behind a `priceData?.pricePerUnit &&`
40	    // guard, so `basePrice` is never actually undefined when this renders. Typed as required to
41	    // satisfy `<FormattedNumber value={basePrice} />`'s `number | bigint` prop under strict null
42	    // checks, without inventing a fallback value the base file never had.
43	    basePrice: number
44	}
45	
46	const PricePerItem = ({currency, basePrice}: PricePerItemProps) => {
47	    return (
48	        <Text fontSize={{base: '12px', lg: '14px'}}>
49	            <FormattedNumber style="currency" currency={currency} value={basePrice} />
50	            <FormattedMessage
51	                defaultMessage="ea"
52	                id="price_per_item.label.each"
53	                description="Abbreviated 'each', follows price per item, like $10/ea"
54	            />
55	        </Text>
56	    )
57	}
58	
59	type ItemPriceProps = {
60	    currency: string
61	    align?: string
62	    baseDirection?: string
63	} & Record<string, any>
64	
65	/**
66	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
67	 * pricing, taking into account applied discounts as well as base item prices.
68	 */
69	const ItemPrice = ({currency, align = 'right', baseDirection = 'column', ...props}: ItemPriceProps) => {
70	    console.log('[overrides] item-price.tsx')
71	    const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant()
72	    const {price, priceAfterItemDiscount} = variant
73	    const isASet = variant?.type?.set
74	    const isMaster = variant?.type?.master
75	    let priceData
76	    // When variant has basket pricing, we should prioritize these prices for displaying
77	    // since they may have take promotion/discount into account
78	    // NOTE: try NOT to re-calculate these values since basket-level discount is complicated
79	    if (variant?.itemId) {
80	        priceData = {
81	            currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount,
82	            // we don't want to show strikethrough price for cart since listPrice is not available via basket pricing
83	            listPrice: null,
84	            pricePerUnit: variant?.pricePerUnit,
85	            isASet,
86	            isMaster,
87	            isRange: isASet || isMaster || false,
88	            isOnSale: price > priceAfterItemDiscount
89	        }
90	    } else {
91	        // for wishlist page we extract price info from variant/product obj
92	        priceData = getPriceData(variant)
93	    }
94	    const isDesktop = useBreakpointValue({base: false, lg: true})
95	
96	    return (
97	        <Stack
98	            textAlign={align}
99	            direction={baseDirection}
100	            justifyContent={align === 'left' ? 'flex-start' : 'flex-end'}
101	            alignItems="baseline"
102	            spacing={priceData?.isOnSale ? 0 : 1}
103	            wrap="nowrap"
104	            {...props}
105	        >
106	            {!isDesktop && variant?.quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (
107	                <PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />
108	            )}
109	
110	            {variant?.itemId ? (
111	                <DisplayPrice
112	                    labelForA11y={variant?.name}
113	                    currency={currency}
114	                    priceData={priceData}
115	                    listPriceProps={{fontSize: 'sm'}}
116	                />
117	            ) : (
118	                <DisplayPrice
119	                    labelForA11y={variant?.name}
120	                    currency={currency}
121	                    priceData={priceData}
122	                    quantity={variant?.quantity}
123	                    listPriceProps={{fontSize: 'sm'}}
124	                />
125	            )}
126	
127	            {isDesktop && variant?.quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (
128	                <PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />
129	            )}
130	        </Stack>
131	    )
132	}
133	
134	export default ItemPrice

Here's the compiled prep for Backlog Refinement. All 11 came from Miraal's list, all sit under Epic SFCC-18 "Pricing," and all are already status "Tech design," targeted at Sprint 6 (21 Sep – 5 Oct — starts in 4 days). I read each Jira issue in full (comments, links, changelogs), checked Confluence, and cross-checked against this repo's PRD, integration docs, and actual current code.

## Before the room — three things that change how several of these read

**Two Confluence design trackers now disagree with each other, and I only found the second one mid-session.** The old 04.2 tracker (page 258801666) still shows individual Pricing-epic rows ("Was/Now Price Display," "DDP/DDU Duties Messaging") as Pending/Pending. A newer one, **04.72 (page 408944644)**, marks the *whole Pricing epic* "no design required." Both are live pages. Whoever's used to checking 04.2 will walk in thinking nothing is designed; whoever checks 04.72 will think everything's covered. Neither is obviously wrong, but they can't both be the answer for the same ticket — worth resolving which one the room trusts before using either to call a story ready.

**Four tickets not on Miraal's list are already gating four that are on it**: SFCC-816 (Cart Summary Component — blocks SFCC-826 and SFCC-280), SFCC-878 (Avalara Integration — blocks SFCC-462), SFCC-43 (Tax Display & Tax Class Config, possible scope overlap with SFCC-462), and SFCC-921 (Checkout DDP/DDU Disclaimer, the checkout-side sibling of SFCC-826). None of these are done. Worth checking whether Miraal's list was meant to be the complete Sprint 6 pricing scope, or just the ones he had visibility on.

**`overrides/app/pages/cart/` does not exist in this repo at all**, and neither does `display-price/`, `order-summary/`, or `promo-code/` as Zimmermann overrides — confirmed directly against the filesystem, not inferred. Several of these stories assume a cart page or a styled price component that simply isn't built yet.

---

## FED / UI stories — full refinement

### SFCC-826 — Cart Duties & Taxes Text Display
**Not sizeable yet — two open questions are load-bearing, not cosmetic.**
- Lens: real FE impact (a conditional cart text block), but the mechanism has two live problems: (1) Miraal's own Jira comment thread (1–3 Sep) settled on "per storefront is sufficient," but the actual DDP/DDU country list mixes both within the same storefront (e.g. EU Intl, HK) — per-storefront literally cannot satisfy the AC as written. (2) The AC requires the list and message text to live in a single Contentful "UI Copy" entry, but that content type is a flat string field with a 256-char limit — it has no array field for a 50-country list.
- Axes: behaviour is unusually well-specified (the country list checks out against Confluence's canonical market table); a11y has zero mention of how a dynamically shown/hidden message gets announced; data is solid except for the schema mismatch above.
- Design: mixed signal, see the tracker conflict above; a Figma link and screenshot exist on the ticket but weren't opened.
- Questions: **[BA — Miraal]** did the "repurposed for additional complexities" pass on 9 Sep already fix the per-storefront vs per-country mismatch? **[Dev — Integration lead]** extend `uiCopy` or use the `footerConfig`-style array pattern instead — this is schema-design, not a Squad A call. **[BA — Squad A lead]** SFCC-816 (the cart container itself) is still Tech design — sequencing risk.

### SFCC-468 — Global-e Duties & Taxes Messaging (PDP)
**Blocked on a data-source decision, not on design.**
- Lens: behaviourally clear and low complexity in isolation, but the actual data source for "is this country DDP or DDU" is unspecified — this is the exact open item `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md` §9 already flags, and it's still unanswered in Confluence's "Global-e Open Questions" page too.
- Axes: no desktop/mobile breakpoint criterion (SFCC-826 has one, this doesn't — inconsistent); no a11y criterion for the dynamic message either.
- Design: not the blocker here — the newer 04.72 tracker marks Pricing "no design required," on schedule for Sprint 6. The ticket's own reference image says to place the message "below Find in Boutique," which isn't built yet (known gap, already logged in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`) — minor, not a blocker.
- Questions: **[Dev — Integration lead]** should this share SFCC-826's Contentful mechanism, or get its own? **[BA]** is "selected ship-to country" here the same signal as SFCC-826's "active Global-e session country" — if not, PDP and cart could disagree mid-visit.

### SFCC-464 — Sale Price Display (Was/Now, all surfaces)
**Too broad to size as one story.**
- Lens: the AC lists 8 surfaces (Homepage, PLP, PDP, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, order history) but the Homepage line is **struck through in the raw Jira field** — retracted after Dani Rivett noted "we don't have pricing show on the Homepage" — yet the description text still lists it. That's a live contradiction inside the ticket itself, not something I'm inferring.
- Reality check per surface: PDP/PLP/checkout exist and already carry real price logic. Cart doesn't exist yet. Wishlist and order history don't exist as pages at all, and per the 04.72 tracker their own design isn't finalised until Sep 21, dev-ready Oct 5 — after Sprint 6 starts.
- Axes: "Was" = RRP logic is clear, but PRC-12 (final-sale attribute) and PRC-13 (what AP21's `MarkdownStatus` values should even mean) are both still open in the PRD — so "a sale entry is active" isn't fully defined yet. A11y: the "Now" green has **no confirmed hex value** — Confluence's own note says "waiting on Jon... need a nice green and red" — so contrast can't be checked against WCAG 2.2 AA at all right now, not just unconfirmed.
- Design: no surface has a locked visual today.
- Questions: **[BA — Miraal/Hazel]** Homepage — struck-through AC or the description, which is authoritative? **[Dev/BA]** `display-price` (the component that would actually render this) is Squad-B-owned per `protectedFiles.md` and has never been overridden — this Squad-A-labelled story would create it first; who owns that build? **[Design]** confirmed green hex, checked for contrast? **[BA]** SFCC-280 already covers the cart's dynamic version of this same treatment — should 464 exclude cart recalculation to avoid double-building it?
- **Suggest splitting**: PDP/PLP/cart/checkout (buildable once colour + the SFCC-37 pricebook dependency land) vs. wishlist/order history (blocked on pages that don't exist and designs not due until late Sprint 6).

### SFCC-463 — Price Display Consistency (currency/formatting, all surfaces)
**Not ready — one open ownership question, one scope conflict.**
- Lens: same 8-ish-surface breadth as SFCC-464 (they're near-duplicates in surface list, no Jira link between them despite both being Squad-A/same-sprint). 7 of 8 surfaces are actually low-risk: currency formatting already works today via `react-intl`'s `FormattedNumber`, confirmed used consistently across PDP, PLP, cart, checkout, and order history/confirmation — nothing needs building there.
- The real gap: this ticket is formally **blocked by SFCC-46** in Jira (linked 2 Sep), and SFCC-46's own description says PWA rendering is "deferred to the relevant frontend epics" — meaning SFCC-463 is supposed to be the one that builds the bridge from BM-configured formatting rules to the renderer. Nobody has. Emma Kirwan asked about this in a comment on SFCC-46 on 10 Sep and it's still unanswered.
- The other gap: "recently viewed full history" (AC #8, added 14 Sep) doesn't exist as a page anywhere, and the Design Tracker itself has an open question on whether that page should even show price at all.
- Questions: **[BA/Dev — Miraal + Emma Kirwan]** does SFCC-463 own building the BM-config-to-renderer bridge, or does that need its own story? **[BA — Miraal]** resolve the "recently viewed" scope conflict before it's in this AC. **[PO]** sequence with SFCC-464 — they'll touch the same files.

### SFCC-462 — US Tax Display (exclusive pricing + checkout)
**Not ready — real regression risk, plus a hard unbuilt dependency.**
- Lens: splits cleanly into a BM admin toggle (near-zero PWA work) and a genuinely PWA-visible half (no tax-inclusive label on US browse surfaces, a TAX line in the checkout order summary). The order-summary half is smaller than it sounds — the base `order-summary` component **already** renders an unconditional Tax row off `basket.taxTotal`.
- That's exactly the regression risk: **that Tax row has no site/locale gate today** — it renders unconditionally for everyone. AU and EU are confirmed tax-inclusive storefronts; nothing in this ticket, its comments, or the Design Tracker addresses how AU/EU/UK stay unaffected.
- Also blocked on **SFCC-878** (Avalara Integration — not built, so there's no real `taxTotal` to verify against yet), and possibly duplicates **SFCC-43**'s BM-config scope.
- Questions: **[BA — Miraal]** does SFCC-462 duplicate SFCC-43? **[Dev — Integration lead / order-summary owner]** confirm AU/EU/UK won't regress — this needs an explicit answer, not an assumption. **[Dev]** can this be dev-ready before SFCC-878 ships `taxTotal`?

### SFCC-280 — Cart Behaviour, Price Recalculation
**Blocked on SFCC-816 — the display logic itself is small.**
- Lens: this is genuinely low-complexity once unblocked — the ticket's own text confirms basket recalculation is OOTB SFCC behaviour, this story is only the Was/Now *display* of it. The "silent, next-load-only" requirement (no real-time recalculation needed) is already satisfied for free by this app's existing React Query defaults (10s stale time, refetch on remount) — no polling or websocket needed.
- The blocker: same as SFCC-826 — no cart page exists yet (SFCC-816, a different epic, still Tech design). Worth noting: SFCC-280 isn't even formally linked to SFCC-816 in Jira today — the dependency only exists in prose, which is itself worth fixing regardless of the refinement outcome.
- Axes: no conflict with existing toast/notification patterns (checked — `useToast` is only used for add-to-bag errors elsewhere). A11y: open question — a silent visual-only price swap may need a live-region announcement for WCAG 2.2 AA; not addressed anywhere.
- Questions: **[BA — PO/Scrum Lead]** should this be pulled into Sprint 6 before SFCC-816 ships — cross-epic sequencing call, not a component one. **[Dev]** will SFCC-816's basket shape carry the was/now fields this needs, or does 280 need to define that contract itself?

---

## Not FED work — flagging for the room, not refining in depth

These four all read, on their Jira AC, as pure SFCC Business Manager configuration or a backend integration job — zero PWA/React component in scope. I verified rather than assumed for the first two; the last three I'm calling from the AC text alone (no agent dispatched — didn't want to spend the room's time chasing Confluence/Figma for screens the PWA repo doesn't touch).

- **SFCC-481** (Price Search Index) — confirmed no PWA change: the existing PLP/search sort and price-filter components are already fully data-driven off whatever the SFCC search index returns. This is entirely an SFCC search-cartridge/index config task.
- **SFCC-46** (Currency Display Formatting) — confirmed no PWA change, and confirmed *correctly* split in the tickets themselves (it explicitly defers rendering to SFCC-463). The real gap is upstream: a linked subtask (SFCC-944) found that the actual per-currency formatting values don't exist as a consolidated spec anywhere yet.
- **SFCC-47** (Global-e FX & Pricing Job) — a nightly SFCC↔Global-e batch job with a Business Manager manual-trigger option. No shopper-facing UI described anywhere in the AC.
- **SFCC-45** (Currency Conversion Approach Configuration) — a Business Manager screen (conversion approach per currency, rounding rules, import/export). No PWA component in the AC.
- **SFCC-44** (Country-Currency Mapping) — a Business Manager mapping screen. The AC's shopper-facing outcome ("correct pricebook is served") is just SFCC picking the right pricebook — nothing for the PWA to build differently.

If any of these actually need FED involvement I'm not seeing from the ticket text, that itself is worth a quick "no FE work, correct?" confirmation with Miraal rather than silently dropping them.

content.text:
**SFCC-743 is the reusable component; SFCC-80 is the PLP page story that's supposed to be built on top of it** — and there's a formal Jira link confirming that: SFCC-743 **blocks** SFCC-80.

**What each one actually is:**
- **SFCC-743 — "Product Card Group – PWA Component"** (Epic SFCC-2, "PWA Kit Components" — a components epic, not a page epic). Builds a generic, reusable `product-card-group` React component: a labelled row of `ProductCard`s (SFCC-236, already Done) with a `display` prop (3/4/6 cards), a `size` prop (Desktop/Mobile), and an optional title+link header. It's explicitly meant for reuse across PDP ("More from this category," "Recommended for you"), Homepage, and PLP — it doesn't own product data or navigation, just renders whatever array it's handed.
- **SFCC-80 — "PLP UI - Product Grid Structure"** (Epic SFCC-6, "Product Listing Page (PLP)"). This is the actual category-page grid: 4-column desktop / 3-column tablet / 2-column mobile, a 36-grid-position budget that shrinks to make room for editorial inserts, and "View More" pagination that appends without a full reload. Its own description says outright: *"The PLP grid itself is not a component... the product group grid component is covered in SFCC-743."*

So the intent is: SFCC-80 is the page assembling itself out of the block SFCC-743 delivers, rather than being its own bespoke grid.

**Where that intent gets shaky — worth raising before either gets built:**
SFCC-743's prop shape doesn't obviously fit what SFCC-80 needs. SFCC-743 is a small, fixed-count shelf (`display: 3, 4, 6`, `size: Desktop, Mobile`, plus tablet only bolted on later via a comment — "when `display=4`, tablet shows 3 to avoid an orphan card"). SFCC-80 needs a full paginated grid with its own breakpoint model (4/3/2 columns), a 36-position budget, and "View More" appending more results. Nothing in SFCC-743's AC mentions pagination, appending, or a 36-item budget. Either SFCC-743 needs more scope than it currently has, or SFCC-80 ends up writing its own grid/pagination logic around repeated SFCC-743 instances — and right now nothing in either ticket says which.

**Two more things worth checking before you rely on this link:**
- SFCC-743's Jira status is **"Blocked"** — but the only comment thread about why (Jasmijn asking, Kiera replying "I can't think of anything outstanding... don't think it's blocked essentially," 10 Sep) never got resolved. If that status is stale, it's quietly holding up SFCC-80 for no real reason.
- SFCC-743 is scheduled in **Sprint 6**; SFCC-80 isn't in any sprint yet. Consistent with "blocker ships first," but worth confirming that's deliberate rather than SFCC-80 simply not having been scheduled.

Want me to run these two through the full refinement lens (design status, axes, readiness call) the way I did the pricing batch, or was this just the relationship question?

**If nothing gets sorted out before someone picks up SFCC-80, it'll stall in the first day of work.** It's linked to a component (SFCC-743) that doesn't actually do what it needs to do yet, and that component is sitting in a "Blocked" status that nobody can currently explain.

**Why:** SFCC-743 builds a small, reusable shelf — a row of 3, 4, or 6 product cards with a title, the kind of thing you'd use for "Recommended for you." SFCC-80 is the actual PLP grid — a completely different shape of problem: full category grid, 4/3/2 columns depending on device, "View More" to load more, up to 36 slots. SFCC-80's own ticket says "use SFCC-743 for this," but SFCC-743 was never built to handle a grid, pagination, or that many items. The link between them is real in Jira, but the two components don't actually fit together the way the link implies.

**Fix, before Sprint 6 picks this up:** two things need answers, not assumptions.
1. Get whoever owns SFCC-743 to explain the "Blocked" status — even its own assignee said in the comments she doesn't think it's blocked. If it's stale, clear it; if it's real, name the reason.
2. Get an explicit call on whether SFCC-743 gets extended to handle grid/pagination, or SFCC-80 just builds its own grid logic and stops relying on SFCC-743 for this part. Right now that's undecided, and whoever builds SFCC-80 will have to guess.
